title: Flexible navigation and content
learningObjectives: Explain flexible navigation and content and apply responsive design principles.

understand.concept: Responsive navigation should preserve access to every destination while adapting its presentation. Common patterns include wrapping navigation links, collapsing into an accessible disclosure control, and changing spacing or arrangement at content-led breakpoints.
understand.whyItMatters: Do not hide navigation without providing a usable alternative. A collapsed menu needs an accessible button, clear expanded state, keyboard support, and a sensible focus order. Long translated labels must be tested.
understand.analogy: Navigation is a map of destinations; its shape can change, but every route should remain discoverable and usable.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; responsive behaviour is determined by CSS layout and viewport/container conditions.

explain.narrative: The links wrap naturally and stack on very narrow screens. All destinations remain visible and keyboard reachable.

practise.guidedTask: Test the navigation with long translated labels. Build a collapsed version using a real button with aria-expanded and keyboard-operable menu behaviour.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive page section and test it at narrow, medium, and wide viewport sizes, including longer labels.
hints: Use the browser responsive viewport tools.
Check horizontal overflow and text scaling.
Keep keyboard access and semantic structure intact.

questions.prompt: What must a responsive navigation preserve when its layout changes?
options: Access to every destination and keyboard usability
questions.answer: Access to every destination and keyboard usability
questions.explanation: Responsive navigation must keep destinations discoverable and operable.

questions.prompt: What should be included in responsive testing?
options: Different viewport sizes and longer content
questions.answer: Different viewport sizes and longer content
questions.explanation: Responsive defects often appear at intermediate widths or with expanded content.
